title: Computed singular values and rank revealing factorizations

items.title: Householder bidiagonalization and its finite precision status
items.statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$, where $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$. Put $p=\min(m,n)$ and $M=\max(m,n)$. If $m\ge n$, set $C=A$; if $m<n$, set $C=A^*$. Thus $C\in\mathbb F^{M\times p}$.

Save the input as $C_0=C$ and initialize $U=I_M$, $V=I_p$, and empty ordered lists of stored local left and right transformations. For $k=1,\ldots,p$, in this order:

1. Let $x=C_{k:M,k}$. If $x=0$, use the identity left transformation. Otherwise choose $\phi=x_1/|x_1|$ when $x_1\ne0$ and $\phi=1$ when $x_1=0$, set $\alpha=-\phi\|x\|_2$, $v=x-\alpha e_1$, and $h=v/\|v\|_2$. Use the Householder reflector $H=I-2hh^*$ on rows $k:M$. Update $C\leftarrow H^*C$ on those rows and append this local transformation to the left list. In exact arithmetic update $U\leftarrow U\operatorname{diag}(I_{k-1},H)$. In finite precision update columns $k:M$ of the dense accumulator $U$ by right application of the same stored local reflector data, using the separate-block branch of [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]] and making no target-zero write to $U$.
2. If $k<p$, let $y=C_{k,k+1:p}^*$. If $y=0$, use the identity right transformation. Otherwise apply the same phase and normalization rule to $y$ to form the Householder reflector $G$, then apply $C\leftarrow C\operatorname{diag}(I_k,G)$ and append this local transformation to the right list. In exact arithmetic update $V\leftarrow V\operatorname{diag}(I_k,G)$. In finite precision update columns $k+1:p$ of the dense accumulator $V$ by right application of the same stored local reflector data, using the separate-block branch of [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]] and making no target-zero write to $V$.

Set $B$ to the leading $p\times p$ block of the final work matrix $C$, and return $B,U,V$ together with the ordered local transformation lists.

In finite precision, each left/right reflector uses [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]], including its real/complex scaled formation, range checks and exact target-column/row zero writes. This is the arithmetic realization of the exact steps above. A zero active vector takes the identity branch. Any helper `range-failure`, invalid operation, nonfinite value, or nonzero exact intermediate outside the normal range returns `range-failure` with the partial factors and stored local transformations; otherwise return `success`, $B,U,V$, the ordered stored local transformations, the reconstruction residual $\|C_0-U\begin{bmatrix}B\\0\end{bmatrix}V^*\|_F$, and the two orthogonality residuals $\|U^*U-I\|_F$ and $\|V^*V-I\|_F$. The reconstruction uses the saved input $C_0$, not the overwritten work matrix. The exact products of the stored unitary representatives are the theoretical factors; the dense finite-precision accumulators are rounded and their residuals are computed quantities, not certified bounds by themselves. Matrix residuals use the Frobenius norm defined in [[def-frobenius-matrix-norm]].

items.title: Strong rank-revealing QR with finite swaps and explicit statuses
items.statement:
Input a real or complex matrix $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$ with $m\ge n$, a target $k$ with $0\le k<n$, a factor $f\ge1$, and a finite swap cap $S\in\mathbb N\cup\{0\}$. The exact-arithmetic version is specified below. A finite-precision implementation uses the same branches, tests finiteness after each operation, and returns `range-failure` if a required quantity is nonfinite.

1. If $A$ is not full column rank, return `rank-deficient-input`. Otherwise initialize a column permutation $\Pi$ and the full column-pivoted QR factorization $A\Pi=QR$, where $Q\in\mathbb F^{m\times m}$ is unitary and $R\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$ is upper trapezoidal. At each pivot choose a remaining column of maximal residual $2$-norm, resolving ties by the smallest original column index. Partition $R=\begin{bmatrix}R_{11}&R_{12}\\0&R_{22}\end{bmatrix}$ after the first $k$ rows and columns. Do not return the reduced QR form. The selected first $k$ columns then have a nonsingular leading block. For $k=0$, return this full factorization with `success`.
2. For $k>0$, refactor the current fixed column order in the full QR form, without further pivoting whenever needed, using unitary Householder or Givens transformations. If the selected leading block is singular, return `singular-selected-block`.
3. Form $X=R_{11}^{-1}R_{12}$. For $1\le i\le k$ let $\omega_i=\|e_i^*R_{11}^{-1}\|_2$; for $1\le j\le n-k$ let $\gamma_j=\|R_{22}(:,j)\|_2$. Define the swap score $s_{ij}=\bigl(|X_{ij}|^2+(\omega_i\gamma_j)^2\bigr)^{1/2}$.
4. If $\max_{i,j}|X_{ij}|>f$, choose the lexicographically first pair attaining the largest $|X_{ij}|$. Otherwise, if $\max_{i,j}s_{ij}>f$, choose the lexicographically first pair attaining the largest score. If neither inequality holds, return `success` and the factors, permutation, $X$, and maximum score. The first branch retains the usual coefficient-triggered swap; the second controls the trailing residual needed for the strong spectral comparison.
5. When a violating pair was chosen, if the swap count is already $S$, return `swap-budget-exhausted` with the current partial factors. Otherwise interchange the chosen selected and trailing columns, restore triangular form with Givens rotations, increment the swap count, and return to step 2.

The statuses are `success`, `rank-deficient-input`, `singular-selected-block`, `swap-budget-exhausted`, and `range-failure`. In particular, ordinary column-pivoted QR is only the initialization: the procedure does not assert that its output alone satisfies the strong bounds. Both exact and finite-precision outputs use the full factor shape. A finite-precision `success` is a candidate until the following certificate is verified. Retain the ordered local transformation data representing an exact unitary product $W$ separately from the rounded dense $Q$. Let $\widehat R$ denote the returned upper trapezoidal matrix. A certificate consists of a nonsingular $\widehat R_{11}$, rigorous upper bounds $b_{ij}$ on the exact real numbers $\bigl(|(\widehat R_{11}^{-1}\widehat R_{12})_{ij}|^2+\|e_i^*\widehat R_{11}^{-1}\|_2^2\|\widehat R_{22}(:,j)\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}$, and $\varepsilon\ge0$ with $\|A\Pi-W\widehat R\|_2\le\varepsilon$. All $b_{ij}\le f$ are required. For $k=0$ there are no score or inverse conditions. The bounds must account for arithmetic and input representation; ordinary rounded score and residual evaluations do not constitute this certificate. Exact arithmetic on represented data or validated outward enclosures may establish it. If certification is unavailable or a bound exceeds its threshold, report `uncertified` for the certificate, retaining the algorithm status and all candidate outputs.

items.title: Singular values contract under left and right multiplication
Singular values are Lipschitz in the spectral norm
Spectral numerical rank counts singular values above threshold over R or C
Finite budget implicit shifted QR for bidiagonal singular values
items.statement:
Input the original $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$, the successful output record of [[alg-householder-bidiagonalization]] for $C=A$ if $m\ge n$ and $C=A^*$ otherwise, a deflation tolerance $\tau\ge0$, and a finite nonnegative integer sweep budget $N$. The reduction record supplies the upper bidiagonal work matrix $B_0$, dense accumulators $U_B,V_B$, and ordered stored local transformation data. Initialize $B=B_0$, the sweep accumulators $U_\Sigma,V_\Sigma$ to identities of order $p=\min(m,n)$, empty ordered left/right transformation lists, an empty deflation record, a pass counter $t=0$, and a sweep counter $s=0$. Write the diagonal as $d_i$ and superdiagonal as $e_i$, and set $e_0=0$.

At the start of each pass, set $t\leftarrow t+1$, set $e_i$ to zero and append $(t,i,e_i^{old})$ to the deflation record whenever $|e_i|\le\tau(|d_i|+|d_{i+1}|)$. The corresponding additive matrix change has entry $-e_i^{old}$ at $(i,i+1)$ and zero elsewhere. Record any later non-target sparsity cleanup the same way with its row, column, and old value. The zero entries split the active blocks. If every active block has size one, stop with `converged`. Otherwise process the active blocks in increasing order of $\ell$, skipping singleton blocks. Before each block sweep, if $s=N$, stop with `budget-exhausted`; otherwise form only the tridiagonal entries of $T=B^*B$ on that block: $T_{ii}=|d_i|^2+|e_{i-1}|^2$ and $T_{i,i+1}=\overline{d_i}e_i$. Choose $\mu$ to be the eigenvalue of the trailing Hermitian block $\begin{bmatrix}T_{r-1,r-1}&T_{r-1,r}\\T_{r,r-1}&T_{rr}\end{bmatrix}$ closest to $T_{rr}$, resolving a tie by the smaller eigenvalue. If the leading pivot $d_\ell$ is zero or has magnitude at most $\tau\max(|e_{\ell-1}|,|e_\ell|)$, use the zero-shift branch $\mu=0$ and choose the initial right Givens factor $G_\ell$ so that $(d_\ell,e_\ell)G_\ell=(\rho,0)$, avoiding division by the small or zero diagonal.

In the ordinary branch choose the first right Givens factor $G_\ell$ so that $G_\ell^*(T_{\ell\ell}-\mu,T_{\ell+1,\ell})^T=(\rho,0)^T$, where $T_{\ell+1,\ell}=\overline{e_\ell}d_\ell$. In either branch, apply $B\leftarrow BG_\ell$, update columns $\ell,\ell+1$ of $V_\Sigma$ by right multiplication by this same stored rotation, and append its exact unitary representative to the right list. For $j=\ell,\ldots,r-1$, choose a left Givens factor $H_j$ so that $H_j^*(B_{j,j},B_{j+1,j})^T=(\rho,0)^T$; apply it to rows $j,j+1$, update columns $j,j+1$ of $U_\Sigma$ by right multiplication by this same stored rotation, and append its exact unitary representative to the left list. If $j<r-1$, choose a right Givens factor $G_{j+1}$ so that $(B_{j,j+1},B_{j,j+2})G_{j+1}=(\rho,0)$; apply it to columns $j+1,j+2$, update the corresponding columns of $V_\Sigma$ by right multiplication by this same stored rotation, and append its exact unitary representative to the right list. Continue until the bulge reaches the active block endpoint. A zero annihilation vector uses the identity rotation. In finite precision each Givens formation/update uses [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]], conjugate-transposed as needed for the stated left/right orientation; accumulator multiplications use the same stored local data but omit all target-zero writes. The dense accumulator multiplications follow the operationwise arithmetic model, while the ordered lists retain the exact unitary representatives used in analysis. Target zero writes to $B$ are included in their local error bounds. The initial shift-vector rotation does not zero an unrelated entry of $B$. Each Givens factor is chosen using [[def-real-and-complex-givens-transformations]] and its annihilation guarantee in [[thm-householder-reflectors-and-givens-transformations-are-unitary-and-annihilate-targeted-entries]].

After each processed block, increment $s$ by one. Once all current active blocks have been processed, start a new pass. If any operation, norm or pivot is invalid or nonfinite, or a nonzero exact intermediate is outside the normal range, return `range-failure` with the partial $B$, accumulators, transformation lists, deflation record, and available residual reports. On `budget-exhausted`, return the current $B$, accumulators, transformation lists, deflation record, triplet residuals, and orthogonality residuals. On `converged`, set $B_{\mathrm{final}}=B$ and return it with both dense accumulators, both transformation lists, the deflation record, triplet/orthogonality residuals, and its tall embedding $\overline B_{\mathrm{final}}=\begin{bmatrix}B_{\mathrm{final}}\\0_{M-p,p}\end{bmatrix}$.

For every exit other than `range-failure`, let $B_{\mathrm{out}}$ be the current work matrix, and let $d_i=(B_{\mathrm{out}})_{ii}$. Obtain each candidate value as $\widehat\sigma_i=|d_i|$ by the scaled two-component modulus evaluation (real absolute value is exact). On `converged`, the active-block condition makes $B_{\mathrm{out}}=B_{\mathrm{final}}$ diagonal; after `budget-exhausted`, the diagonal values are estimates only and carry no accuracy claim.

Let $W_B=\operatorname{diag}(U_\Sigma,I_{M-p})$. In exact arithmetic the tall-orientation accumulated factors are $U_C=U_BW_B$ and $V_C=V_BV_\Sigma$. In finite precision form each dense product by row-by-column multiplication, with six-real-operation complex products and sequential componentwise rounded additions under the operationwise model; return `range-failure` if any required intermediate is invalid, nonfinite, or outside the normal range. Their exact theoretical factors are the products represented by the ordered local transformation lists together with the bidiagonal-reduction lists. If $m\ge n$, set $\widehat U=U_C$ and $\widehat V=V_C$; for each nonzero $d_i$, multiply column $i$ of $\widehat U$ by $d_i/|d_i|$ in exact arithmetic, using componentwise division by the successful scaled modulus readout in finite precision. If $m<n$, set $\widehat U=V_C$ and $\widehat V=U_C$; in this wide orientation multiply column $i$ of $\widehat V$ by $d_i/|d_i|$ instead. Sort the candidate values in nonincreasing order, breaking ties by their original diagonal index, and permute the corresponding columns of the returned triplet vectors in the same way; leave $B_{\mathrm{out}}$ and the transformation lists in their algorithmic order. For every candidate triplet $(\widehat\sigma_i,\widehat u_i,\widehat v_i)$, report $\|A\widehat v_i-\widehat\sigma_i\widehat u_i\|_2$ and $\|A^*\widehat u_i-\widehat\sigma_i\widehat v_i\|_2$. Also report $\|\widehat U^*\widehat U-I\|_F$ and $\|\widehat V^*\widehat V-I\|_F$. The reports expose finite-budget and rounding behavior; they do not certify convergence by themselves. Matrix residuals use the Frobenius norm defined in [[def-frobenius-matrix-norm]]. Any additional sparsity cleanup is recorded separately in the deflation record with its discarded-entry perturbation.

items.title: Exact unitary equivalence of Householder bidiagonalization
A strong RRQR column swap multiplies selected volume by its score
Componentwise relative perturbations of bidiagonal matrices control every singular value relatively
Strong RRQR block singular values compare to the full matrix spectrum
Rank-thresholded least squares by the singular value decomposition
items.statement:
Input $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$, $b\in\mathbb F^m$, a rank threshold $\tau\ge0$, and a finite nonnegative integer bidiagonal-QR sweep budget $N$, with $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$; vector residuals use the Euclidean norm of [[def-inner-product-norm]]. Compute the Householder bidiagonal reduction and call the finite-budget bidiagonal QR procedure with deflation tolerance zero and no additional sparsity cleanup. If either procedure returns a failure or budget-exhausted status, return `inconclusive` with its triplet and orthogonality reports and do not claim a least-squares solution.

On exact-arithmetic convergence, use the exact SVD record $A=U\Sigma V^*$ from the returned transformation products and diagonal candidates. Set $q=\#\{i:\sigma_i>\tau\}$, form $A_\tau=U\Sigma_\tau V^*$ and the canonical truncated pseudoinverse $A_\tau^+$ of [[def-truncated-singular-value-pseudoinverse-at-a-declared-threshold]], and compute $x_\tau=A_\tau^+b$. Return $x_\tau$, the declared threshold, $q$, the model residual $\|A_\tau x_\tau-b\|_2$, the original residual $\|Ax_\tau-b\|_2$, and the discarded tail size $\sigma_{q+1}$ (defined as $0$ for $q=p=\min(m,n)$). The strict comparison $\sigma_i>\tau$ is used, so values equal to the threshold are discarded. In finite precision, use singular-value estimates $(\widehat U,\widehat\Sigma,\widehat V)$ to form $\widehat I=\{i:\widehat\sigma_i>\tau\}$, $\widehat A_\tau=\widehat U\widehat\Sigma_\tau\widehat V^*$, and the coordinate candidate $\widehat x=\widehat V\widehat\Sigma_{\widehat I}^{+}\widehat U^*b$, where $\widehat\Sigma_{\widehat I}^{+}$ has diagonal entries $1/\widehat\sigma_i$ for $i\in\widehat I$ and zero otherwise; compute both residuals and label the threshold count `unverified` unless a certified error interval separates every compared value from $\tau$. This finite-precision candidate is not called a certified numerical rank or a minimum-norm least-squares solution.

items.title: Bulge chase preserves bidiagonal singular values
The strong RRQR swap rule terminates after finitely many swaps
Local stable reflectors and rotations give an aggregate SVD backward error
items.statement:
Let $C_0\in\mathbb F^{M\times p}$, $M\ge p$, be the tall orientation used by [[alg-householder-bidiagonalization]], and let $B_J\in\mathbb F^{p\times p}$ be the final bidiagonal-QR work matrix returned by [[alg-implicit-shifted-bidiagonal-qr-with-deflation]]. Set $C_J=\begin{bmatrix}B_J\\0_{M-p,p}\end{bmatrix}\in\mathbb F^{M\times p}$. Suppose the computed bidiagonal reduction and QR sweeps perform $J$ stages, each either an elementary left/right unitary update or an identity update for a deflation/cleanup write. At stage $j$, assume the actual active matrix obeys
$$C_j=L_j^*(C_{j-1}+E_j)R_j+D_j,$$
where $L_j,R_j$ are unitary and $\eta_j\ge0$, $\|E_j\|_F\le\eta_j\|C_{j-1}\|_F$, and $D_j$ is the additive representation of entries discarded by deflation or cleanup at that stage, with $\delta_j=\|D_j\|_F$. A deflation/cleanup write is represented by $L_j=R_j=I$, $E_j=0$, and the recorded additive change $D_j$. The deflation record returned by the algorithm identifies each such entry and its old value, so it determines $D_j$. Then the returned tall transformed matrix $C_J$ satisfies
$$C_0+E=L C_J R^*$$
for unitary accumulated factors $L,R$ and some $E$ with
$$\|E\|_F\le\left(\prod_{j=1}^J(1+\eta_j)-1\right)\|C_0\|_F+\sum_{j=1}^J\delta_j\prod_{\ell=j+1}^J(1+\eta_\ell).$$
If no deflation or other cleanup is performed, every $\delta_j=0$. For the successful scaled arithmetic realization [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]], [[lem-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-local-backward-error]] establishes these hypotheses: choose $\eta_j=\eta_H(r_j)$ for Householder updates, $\eta_j=\eta_G$ for Givens updates with an actual target zero write, and its smaller separate-block coefficient when no matrix entry is overwritten. This covers real/complex left and right updates. Every additional discarded entry is included in $D_j$. Rounded dense accumulators remain separate from these exact represented products.
items.strategy:
1.1 Iterating the norm inequality from [A1] gives $\|C_j\|_F\le(1+\eta_j)\|C_{j-1}\|_F+\delta_j$. Induction from $C_0$ yields $\|C_j\|_F\le\left(\prod_{r=1}^j(1+\eta_r)\right)\|C_0\|_F+\sum_{r=1}^j\delta_r\prod_{s=r+1}^j(1+\eta_s)$: the base case $j=0$ is equality, and the one-step inequality multiplies every prior term by $1+\eta_j$ and adds $\delta_j$. [A1, F3, induction, algebra]

2.1 Unwind each update in the accumulated unitary coordinates supplied by [F1]–[F2]. The original-input perturbation is the sum of each $E_j$ and each $D_j$ transported by products of later unitary factors. Unitary left/right multiplication preserves Frobenius norm, so $\|E\|_F\le\sum_{j=1}^J\eta_j\|C_{j-1}\|_F+\sum_{j=1}^J\delta_j$. Substitute step 1.1. For the $C_0$ terms, $\sum_j\eta_j\prod_{r<j}(1+\eta_r)=\prod_r(1+\eta_r)-1$. For a fixed $\delta_i$, its contribution is $\delta_i\left(1+\sum_{j>i}\eta_j\prod_{i<r<j}(1+\eta_r)\right)=\delta_i\prod_{r>i}(1+\eta_r)$. These identities give the stated bound. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 The same coordinate unwinding gives $C_J= L^*(C_0+E)R$ for products $L,R$ of the unitary update factors, hence $C_0+E=L C_JR^*$. Step 2.1 gives its error bound; setting every $\delta_j=0$ gives the no-deflation case. [step 2.1, F1, F2, algebra]

3.2 For the specified finite-precision algorithm, apply [F5] to each actual update, retaining its range and active-dimension hypotheses. It gives exactly [A1], including each target-zero write. Deflation and any additional discarded entries remain $D_j$, so steps 1.1–3.1 prove the displayed aggregate bound for the concrete implementation. Shift rounding affects which rotation is chosen, not the validity of its unitary backward-error certificate; no unconditional convergence is asserted. [F5, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: The SVD threshold solver gives the unique minimum-norm fit to its truncated model
Computed singular-value error is bounded by backward perturbation plus readout error
items.statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$ and put $C=A$ when $m\ge n$, $C=A^*$ when $m<n$. Suppose a successful computed SVD path in this tall orientation supplies $C+E=\widehat U\begin{bmatrix}\widehat B\\0\end{bmatrix}\widehat V^*$, where $\widehat U\in\mathbb F^{M\times M}$ and $\widehat V\in\mathbb F^{p\times p}$ are the exact unitary products represented by the stored local transformations, $M=\max(m,n)$, $p=\min(m,n)$, and the returned square $\widehat B\in\mathbb F^{p\times p}$ is the diagonal final bidiagonal matrix from [[alg-implicit-shifted-bidiagonal-qr-with-deflation]]. These are the theoretical factors in [[thm-bidiagonal-svd-backward-error-under-local-stability]], separate from the rounded dense accumulators returned for candidate triplets. If the returned values are the exact singular values of $\widehat B$, then for every $1\le i\le p$,
$$|\widehat\sigma_i-\sigma_i(A)|\le\|E\|_2\le\|E\|_F.$$
For actual rounded modulus readout from a diagonal $\widehat B$, let $d_i=\widehat B_{ii}$ and $\epsilon_{\rm read}=((1+u)^4-1)\max(\{0\}\cup\{|d_i|:1\le i\le p\})$ for the successful scaled complex modulus algorithm; use zero for exact real absolute values. Thus $\epsilon_{\rm read}=0$ when $p=0$. After ordering the candidates, the bound is $|\widehat\sigma_i-\sigma_i(A)|\le\|E\|_2+\epsilon_{\rm read}$. This assertion applies to a successful, fully reduced result; a finite-budget `budget-exhausted` output has residual reports but no such accuracy conclusion.
items.strategy:
1.1 By [F1], $C+E=\widehat U\begin{bmatrix}\widehat B\\0\end{bmatrix}\widehat V^*$. The tall matrix $\begin{bmatrix}\widehat B\\0\end{bmatrix}$ has the singular values of $\widehat B$, since its adjoint times itself is $\widehat B^*\widehat B$; unitary invariance in [F3] therefore gives the ordered singular values $s_i$ for $C+E$. By [F4], $C$ and $A$ have the same $p$ singular values. [F1, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 Apply [F2] to $C$ and $C+E$. It gives $|\sigma_i(C+E)-\sigma_i(C)|\le\|E\|_2$; step 1.1 identifies these singular values with $s_i$ and $\sigma_i(A)$, respectively, and [F3] gives $\|E\|_2\le\|E\|_F$. [step 1.1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.2 A scaled modulus of two real components has relative norm factors between $(1-u)^4$ and $(1+u)^4$, by expanding the two scaling operations, square products and sum, square root and rescaling. Hence each rounded magnitude differs from $|d_i|$ by at most $\epsilon_{\rm read}$. If two finite lists differ coordinatewise by at most $\epsilon$, their ordered lists do too: otherwise at the violating rank the count of entries above or below the corresponding threshold contradicts the coordinatewise bounds. Apply this to the diagonal magnitudes and combine with step 2.1. For exact readout $\widehat\sigma_i=s_i$ the first bound follows already from step 2.1; for rounded readout the additional modulus allowance gives the stated extension. Real sign removal is exact. [F5, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Scaled real and complex Householder and Givens update arithmetic
items.statement:
**Scalar execution order.** These conventions expand every arithmetic
expression below into a fixed finite scalar schedule; they do not execute the
exact theoretical representatives. Visit vector indices increasingly and matrix
columns increasingly, with row indices increasing within each column. Visit the
real component before the imaginary component. For a complex vector $z$, its
real-component list is $(\Re z_1,\Im z_1,\ldots,\Re z_r,\Im z_r)$.
Evaluate displayed assignments in their written order and nested operations
from the inside out, left operand before right operand. For inputs $a+ib$ and
$c+id$ with real components $a,b,c,d$, a complex product uses
rounded real products $ac,bd,ad,bc$, in that order, followed by the rounded real
subtraction $ac-bd$ and rounded imaginary addition $ad+bc$. Do not fuse
operations. Return immediately at the first failing primitive; indices refer
to this expanded order. Copies, sign changes and conjugations are exact.

For a scaled norm, first form every rounded component divided by the common
scale in list order. Then, in that same order, round each component square and
accumulate it: copy the first square to the accumulator, and round each
subsequent accumulator-plus-square addition. Use this same square-and-sum
schedule for the stored-vector squared norm $w$, without scaling. An empty
sum is exact zero and requests no primitive. Apply square root and rescaling
only at their prescribed subsequent stages. The two-component and
four-component norm calls use their displayed component lists in this order.

For the Householder dot row $d$, visit columns $j$ increasingly. For each
column visit $i=1,\ldots,r$, form the declared complex product
$\overline v_iB_{ij}$, copy the first product as the partial dot, then add each
later product by rounded real-component addition followed by rounded
imaginary-component addition. Finish all of $d$ before forming $p$ in
increasing row order, then all of $Z$ in the matrix order above, then all
entries of $B-Z$ in that order. Evaluate both components of the formation of
$v$ and every scalar scaling or division in real-then-imaginary order. A
separate block call uses already stored $v,\widehat\tau$ and the same
$d,p,Z,B-Z$ stages, omitting formation and target overwrite.

For a Givens application, visit columns increasingly and copy the two old
entries before changing either. Compute the upper output first, then the
lower output, each by its two products in written order followed by its
componentwise addition. Each of the prescribed two complex products uses
the six-operation schedule above, including a real coefficient viewed as a
complex number with zero imaginary component. Both outputs use the copied
old entries.
Perform an instructed target zero write only after these outputs. Right
applications execute the stated conjugate-transpose reduction with these
same conventions. No intermediate is reused across different expressions
unless explicitly stored by the procedure.

Use the operationwise real/complex arithmetic model, with six-real-operation complex products and componentwise division by positive real scalars. A scaled norm of a nonzero complex vector first chooses the largest absolute real or imaginary component $s>0$, rounds every real component divided by $s$, sums their rounded squares sequentially, rounds the positive square root, and rounds multiplication by $s$. A norm of already scaled components omits the last multiplication. Zero input has exact norm zero. Reject every nonzero exact intermediate outside the normal range, nonfinite/invalid operation, and nonpositive required norm; return the first range-failure. All sign changes and conjugations are exact.

For a Householder active block $C=[x\;B]$, $x\in\mathbb C^r$, a zero $x$ copies the block with identity action. Otherwise compute $\widehat N$ by the scaled norm. If $x_1=0$ put $\widehat\phi=1$; otherwise compute its modulus $\widehat a$ by its own two-component scaled norm and divide its real and imaginary parts by $\widehat a$. Set $\widehat\alpha=-\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\phi\widehat N)$ using real-scalar component multiplication, and $v=\operatorname{fl}(x-\widehat\alpha e_1)$. Compute $w$ by sequential summation of all $2r$ rounded real component squares of $v$, and $\widehat\tau=\operatorname{fl}(2/w)$. Compute $d=\operatorname{fl}(v^*B)$, $p=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\tau v)$, $Z=\operatorname{fl}(pd)$, and $\widehat B=\operatorname{fl}(B-Z)$. Return $C_+=[\widehat\alpha e_1\;\widehat B]$, writing exact zeros below the target diagonal, and store $v,\widehat\tau$. Its theoretical representative is $H(v)=I-2vv^*/(v^*v)$. For a separate block application omit the column overwrite. For a right step apply these instructions to the conjugate-transposed block and transpose back.

For a Givens target pair $(a,b)$, use the identity when $b=0$, including $(0,0)$. Otherwise choose $\lambda$ as the largest absolute real/imaginary component of $(a,b)$, round $z=a/\lambda$ and $w=b/\lambda$ componentwise, and compute $h$ as the norm of their four already scaled components. If $z\ne0$, compute $n_z$ as the norm of its two components, $\widehat\phi=\operatorname{fl}(z/n_z)$, $c=\operatorname{fl}(n_z/h)$ and $s=\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\phi\overline w)/h)$. If $z=0$, set $c=0$ and $s=\operatorname{fl}(\overline w/h)$. Store $T=\begin{pmatrix}c&s\\-\overline s&c\end{pmatrix}$ and apply it to the chosen two rows using two complex products and one rounded componentwise addition for each output entry. For an actual target column, set its intended annihilated entry to exact zero after the update. The initial shift-vector rotation is formed from the shift vector but applied to the matrix without zeroing an unrelated matrix entry. Right applications use the conjugate-transposed form. Its exact unitary representative is $Q=T/\sqrt{c^2+|s|^2}$; this normalization defines a mathematical representative and is not an additional rounded operation.

These are arithmetic realizations of the canonical Householder and Givens methods. Returned dense transformation accumulators may be rounded; the exact unitary products used in backward-error statements are represented by the stored local data. Additional discarded matrix entries must be recorded separately, including their magnitudes. Their omission is never implicit in a sparsity convention.

items.title: Scaled complex Householder and Givens steps have explicit local backward errors
items.statement:
Use [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]] successfully, with $0<u<1$ and $(r-1)u<1$ for every Householder dimension $r$. For a nonzero Householder column define
$$e=(1+u)^{r+3}-1,\quad a_\phi=\frac{1+u}{(1-u)^4}-1,\quad a_\alpha=(1+a_\phi)(1+e)(1+u)-1,\quad d_v=a_\alpha+u(2+a_\alpha),$$
$$a_\tau=\frac{1+u}{(1-u)^{2r}}-1,\quad g=\frac{1+6u}{1-(r-1)u}-1,\quad c_U=2\bigl((1+a_\tau)(1+u)(1+6u)(1+g)-1\bigr),$$
$$\eta_H(r)=\max\{a_\alpha+8d_v,(1+u)c_U+3u\}.$$
For a Givens step define
$$a_2=\frac{1+u}{(1-u)^2}-1,\quad q=\max\left\{\left(\frac{1+u}{1-u}\right)^3-1,\frac{(1+a_2)(1+6u)(1+u)}{(1-u)^3}-1\right\},$$
$$\epsilon=\sqrt2(7u+6u^2)(1+q),\quad v=q+\epsilon,\quad \eta_G=2v+u+2q.$$
Each complete left update, including its target zero write, has an exact unitary representative $W$ and perturbation $E$ with
$$W(C+E)=C_+,\qquad \|E\|_F\le\eta\|C\|_F,$$
where $\eta=\eta_H(r)$ or $\eta_G$. Identity branches have $E=0$. The corresponding right relation follows by conjugate transposition. For a Givens application without an annihilation overwrite use the smaller coefficient $v$; for a Householder separate-block application use $(1+u)c_U+3u$. All coefficients are explicit and $O(ru)$ or $O(u)$ for fixed dimensions.
items.strategy:
1.1 A complex product's real/imaginary error is at most $2(2u+u^2)|z||w|\le6u|z||w|$: bound each of its four real products and then its two component additions. A sequential complex dot of length $r$ therefore has error at most $[6u+\gamma_{r-1}(1+6u)]\sum_i|z_i||w_i|=g\sum_i|z_i||w_i|$. These expansions include exact zeros. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 A scaled norm with $2r$ real components has its positive squared sum multiplied termwise by between $(1-u)^{2r+2}$ and $(1+u)^{2r+2}$, including two scaling factors. Square root and rescaling give relative norm error at most $e$. The independently scaled modulus of $x_1$ has lower/upper factors $(1-u)^4,(1+u)^4$, so the phase division error relative to $x_1/|x_1|$ is at most $a_\phi$; when $x_1=0$ it is zero. Thus for $N=\|x\|$, $\alpha_0=-\operatorname{phase}(x_1)N$ and $v_0=x-\alpha_0e_1$, one has $|\widehat\alpha-\alpha_0|\le a_\alpha N$ and $\|v-v_0\|\le d_vN$. For exponents at least one the lower deviation is bounded by the upper by convexity, justifying these two-sided estimates. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 The identity $H(v)^*H(v)=I$ follows by multiplying $I-2vv^*/(v^*v)$. The exact phase choice gives $H(v_0)x=\alpha_0e_1$ and $\|v_0\|\ge N$ by direct inner-product expansion. Normalization gives $\|a/\|a\|-b/\|b\|\|\le2\|a-b\|/\|b\|$; expanding the difference of unit-vector projectors therefore gives $\|H(v)-H(v_0)\|\le8d_v$. The target-column error is at most $(a_\alpha+8d_v)N$. [step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 For Givens formation at stored $z,w$, the norm $h$ has relative factors between $(1-u)^3$ and $(1+u)^3$, since its unscaled four-component squared sum has at most four rounding factors per term. The norm $n_z$ has exponents two. Let $G_0$ be the exact canonical Givens annihilator for $(z,w)$, with coefficients $c_0=|z|/\|(z,w)\|$ and $s_0=(z/|z|)\overline w/\|(z,w)\|$ when $z\ne0$. The phase error is at most $a_2$; the coefficient numerator, denominator, six-operation complex product and division errors therefore give $|c-c_0|\le q c_0$ and $|s-s_0|\le q|s_0|$. If $z=0$, $c=0$ and $s_0=\overline w/|w|$; the smaller bound $(1+u)/(1-u)^3-1\le q$ applies. Hence $\|(c,s)-(c_0,s_0)\|\le q$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The positive real sum defining $w$ has bounds $(1-u)^{2r}\|v\|^2\le w\le(1+u)^{2r}\|v\|^2$. The final division gives $|\widehat\tau\|v\|^2/2-1|\le a_\tau$. The dot-product error in step 1.1, the componentwise real multiplication by $\widehat\tau$ and the final complex multiplication bound the rank-one update error by $c_U\|B\|_F$. Final subtraction adds at most $u(3+c_U)\|B\|_F$. Combine this with step 2.1 over disjoint columns to get the Householder bound. For the zero column take the identity exactly. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 Put $t=\sqrt{c^2+|s|^2}>0$ and $Q=T/t$. Direct multiplication gives $T^*T=t^2I$, so $Q$ is canonical unitary, $\|T-Q\|=|t-1|\le q$ and $\|T\|\le1+q$. Normalization also gives $\|Q-G_0\|\le2q$; differences of canonical blocks have norm equal to the Euclidean norm of their coefficient differences. Each computed output entry has error at most $(7u+6u^2)(|c||C_{1j}|+|s||C_{2j}|)$, by two products and their addition. The absolute coefficient block has norm at most $\sqrt2t$. Thus the raw update differs from $QC$ by at most $v\|C\|_F$. [step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 Scaling introduced $\|\lambda(z,w)-(a,b)\|\le u\|(a,b)\|$. Because $G_0$ annihilates $(z,w)$, its exact target residual for $(a,b)$ is at most $u\|(a,b)\|$; under $Q$ it is at most $(u+2q)\|(a,b)\|$. Writing the rounded target to zero adds at most $(u+2q+v)\|(a,b)\|$ to the raw update discrepancy, so the total is at most $\eta_G\|C\|_F$. No unrelated matrix entry is zeroed for a shift-vector rotation. Identity branches have zero discrepancy. [F1, step 2.2, step 3.2, algebra]

5.1 In every left case choose $E=W^*C_+-C$, with $W=H(v)$ or $Q$; unitarity gives the stated equation and equal error norm. Right updates follow by conjugate transposition and invariance of Frobenius norm. All coefficients are finite explicit functions under the stated conditions, vanish at $u=0$, and have first derivatives bounded by a fixed multiple of the active dimension, proving the asymptotics. [step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra, construct] ∎
